newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli says make life tough for foreign workers.
newsitem.headline: Israeli says make life tough for foreign workers.

text.p: Israeli public security minister Avigdor Kahalani on Tuesday suggested that Israelis should make life tougher for the country's many foreign workers to encourage some of them to leave.
Kahalani said the aim must be "to help send the foreign workers home by not giving them permission to take over every room and every house".
Israel's government last month began considering ways to cut a growing dependence on what officials say are 100,000 legal and 100,000 illegal foreign workers doing jobs unwanted by Jews.
Workers from such countries as Romania, Thailand, Turkey and China now do the low-paying manual labour of Palestinians barred from the Jewish state for security reasons.

The minister, who heads the right-centre Third Way party, said foreign workers should not be able to set up health institutes -- often a euphemism in Israel for massage parlours -- and churches and taverns.
"If it must be made clear to someone that the health institute must be closed, so life is bitter, then his health institute should be closed," he told Israel Radio.
Kahalani said foreign workers must find life uncomfortable in Tel Aviv, where many of them live and work.
Many live in squalid conditions, and Israelis who once welcomed the foreigners now complain they have brought crime.
Before a seven-year Palestinian uprising that began in 1987, as many as 160,000 Arabs from the West Bank and Gaza worked in Israel. Today about 40,000 work in Israel.
